I'll turn it over to Dr. Hughes and Mrs. Bostain. hey good afternoon chair irwin members of the board and dr cashwell as dr cashwell said my name is leslie hughes and i'm the chief learning officer for henrico county public schools joining me today is courtney bustain director of innovation and together we will share an exciting update on esports in henrico county public schools while esports is relatively new it is important to know that it has been widely embraced by teachers administrators and parents At first glance, eSports may look like a recreational gaming, but it is so much more.

It is part of our Life Ready Innovative Pathway, helping students develop durable skills aligned to the Henrico learner profile, including communication, collaboration, problem solving, and digital literacy. Over the past few years, eSports has grown from a small pilot into a meaningful K-12 opportunity that connects student interest with learning, belonging, and future readiness. To understand why this innovative work matters, it is important to begin with a broader vision that guides our work. Esports is grounded in the Division's strategic plan,

Journey to 2030, specifically Goal 1: Academic Achievement, which calls for us to create learning experiences that prepare students not only for graduation, but for life beyond school. That includes helping students engage in meaningful experiences grounded in our core values.

Esports creates another entry point for students to connect, contribute, and grow in ways that are both relevant and engaging. And just as important, Esports aligns directly to the outcomes we want for every learner in HCPS that are embedded in our Henrico Learner Profile, which defines the knowledge and durable skills we want every student to develop over time. When Esports is implemented well, it creates authentic opportunities for students to practice these outcomes in real time.

Students communicate with teammates, collaborate towards shared goals, think critically in fast-paced situations, solve problems, demonstrate character, and learn how to participate responsibly in digital spaces. Esports may look different from a traditional learning experience or activity, but the student outcomes are very much aligned to what we say matters most in Henrico.

At this time, I'll turn the presentation over to Courtney Bostain, who will further explain what what eSports is, how it has been implemented in HCPS, and to share a video with medical school students sharing why they engage in eSports. - Thank you, Dr. Hughes.

Electronic sports or eSports is organized competitive video gaming, typically played in teams within structured supervised environments. In schools, it provides students with opportunities to collaborate, communicate, solve problems, and build confidence.

It also helps students connect with peers develop a stronger sense of belonging within the school community. Beyond schools, eSports has also become a growing and recognized pathway for students. It now connects to college scholarships, academic programs, and career opportunities in areas like technology, media, design, and digital production. For students, that means that eSports can be both a meaningful school experience and a pathway to future opportunities. In Henrico, this work began in 2023 with a clear focus on student engagement and connection. With support from a Henrico Education Foundation

innovation grant, we launched a pilot at three middle schools. From the beginning, the goal was to create spaces where students could connect, collaborate, and build community through a shared interest. Participation quickly exceeded expectations and showed us early on that this could become a meaningful opportunity for our students. Following that early success, the program expanded to the next year to all 12 middle schools. Today, middle school serves as the foundation of eSports in Henrico. For many students, it is their first introduction through structured clubs and team opportunities, and it continues to be a level where we see strong

participation. It has become an entry point for student engagement, skill development, and school connection. That middle school foundation made it possible for us to take the next step into high school this year supported by a virginia department of education grant we are especially proud that esports is now a vhsl sanctioned activity placing it within the same statewide structure as other recognized high school programs in our first year five hcps teams qualified for the vhsl playoffs demonstrating both strong student participation and a successful

program launch at the high school level students continue to build teamwork communication strategy and leadership while also strengthening their connection to school through competition and school pride.

Due to the success we are seeing in the middle and high schools, interest is also growing at the elementary level. In response, we are piloting what this can look like for younger learners in developmentally appropriate student-centered ways. This year, pilots began at Glenlee, Lakeside, and Colonial Trail with additional opportunities supported through grants.

Today we have eight elementary clubs. Our focus is on learning from this pilot and ensuring that any future decisions are made carefully and responsibly. At the elementary level, the emphasis is not on competition, but on structured, team-based experiences where students build foundational skills and develop a strong sense of belonging.

Across all three levels, what stands out the most is the impact this is having on our students. From what we are hearing from students, coaches, and families, one thing is clear. This is creating meaningful engagement for students who are interested in gaming within a structured, school-supported environment.

Students are building skills like communication, collaboration, critical thinking, and problem solving in authentic ways. They are also developing leadership, confidence, and importantly, healthier digital habits by learning how to engage with gaming in balanced and responsible ways.

That is the real value of this work, providing students with another meaningful, structured way to connect, engage, and grow in our schools, while helping them prepare for the realities of the world they are entering. As the impact has grown, we've also seen strong momentum across the division.

Students in schools are taking part in events where they can compete, connect, and celebrate together. We are also seeing individual student success. Earlier this year, a student from Holman Middle School was recognized for winning a regional tournament.
